leads.title: Unsorted remainder of the trial atlas, sorted by a local model with exact-quote checks
leads.question: Can a local model propose a class for the primary outcomes the atlas lexicon leaves unsorted, with every proposal backed by an exact quote from the registry record?
leads.why_it_matters: Without it, a large unsorted remainder would hide part of what CF trials register as their main outcome.

must_not_claim: That a model's class for an outcome is correct because its quote was found in the record.
That the atlas classes measure trial quality.

leads.title: Registry records linked to publications by exact trial-id match, and results-posting baselines
leads.question: For CF trials in the registry, how many have results posted, and how many have a publication that cites their trial id exactly?

sources.ref: Huser and Cimino, PLoS One 2013, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0068409 (journals.plos.org)
sources.note: 23.2 percent is 2,068 of 8,907 completed phase 2 and later trials (data of 7 January 2013) with a link present in PubMed abstracts, not in the registry's reference field. The roughly 44 percent figure comes from the authors' earlier validation study. Both are 2013 snapshots; read through a page-summarising tool; quote not checked against the raw page.

sources.ref: Anderson et al., NEJM 2015, PMID 25760355 (Europe PMC record)
sources.note: General, not CF-specific: among 13,327 trials completed 2008 to 2012, 13.4 percent posted summary results within 12 months and 38.3 percent by 27 September 2013; read through a page-summarising tool; quote not checked against the raw page.

sources.ref: Chen et al., BMJ 2016, PMID 26888209 (Europe PMC record)
sources.note: General, not CF-specific, academic medical centres only: 35.9 percent disseminated within 24 months and 66 percent overall; read through a page-summarising tool; quote not checked against the raw page.

sources.ref: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, studies/metadata, references module
sources.note: Records can carry references with a PMID and a submitter's type label (background, result, derived); read through a page-summarising tool; quote not checked against the raw page.

publication links by trial id (PubMed secondary source id, Europe PMC)

The 2013 figures, or the general baselines, as current rates or as CF rates.
That results posted on the registry and a published paper are the same event.

sources.note: The largest lead-sponsor name holds 110 of 1,072 studies (10.3 percent); 219 names have one study each. Sponsor names as written, not deduplicated. Recomputed independently: yes for the concentration figure (the controlling agent); no for the class mix.

Any judgement of a sponsor; the description is of registered wording only.
